question.text: What is the key difference between STP (Systematic Transfer Plan) and SWP (Systematic Withdrawal Plan)?

answer.text: STP is tax-free while SWP attracts capital gains tax
STP periodically redeems from one scheme and invests into another scheme of the same mutual fund, while SWP periodically redeems units and pays the proceeds to the investor
STP can be set up across different AMCs while SWP is restricted to the same AMC
STP involves only equity schemes while SWP involves only debt schemes

explanation.text: The Logic: A Systematic Transfer Plan (STP) periodically redeems units from one scheme and invests the proceeds into another scheme of the same mutual fund. A Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP) periodically redeems units and pays/withdraws the proceeds for the investor through banking channels. The Trap: STP is not a direct unit transfer between schemes — it is a redemption followed by a fresh investment, which is why switch transactions attract capital-gains treatment. Note: Both STP and SWP involve redemption, so both can have tax consequences for the investor.
